$comment: The interchangeable selling-point matrix for split testing. Every entry names the claim record that must be approved before it may run. Nothing here is pre-approved — see knowledge/claims/README.md and the activation note in this pack's README.
$formats: `label`+`sub` is the light chip form (format `single`). `loud` is the single uppercase line (format `streak`). `spec` is the two-line pair for the three-column spec row (format `panel`) — pre-broken on purpose: left to wrap on their own, one column runs to two lines while the others sit on one and the row looks broken.

thirdparty.label: Third-party tested
thirdparty.sub: independent lab, named on the certificate

variants.$comment: Which points appear together. Vary ONE hypothesis at a time — these are experiments, not rerolls. Each variant competes as an IDEA (rigor vs speed vs price) so the test learns why people buy, not which font won.

hooks.$comment: Headline pairs — clause 1 roman, clause 2 italic with the spectrum gradient. Sentence case, ends in a period. 2–6 words per clause so they survive thumbnail size.

panel.note: Panel headlines name the BIOLOGICAL AXIS, never a benefit and never an outcome.

ctas.$comment: Destination-matched. A product-page CTA is lower friction than the COA library; the COA library gets its own dedicated creative.
ctas.organic: Learn how a COA is read

prohibited.$comment: Deliberately excluded until a sourced claim record exists. Do not resurrect these from old campaign copy — historical prose is not evidence of approval.
claims: Any guarantee, warranty, or money-back promise
Subscribe & Save, "buy 10 get 2 free", or any offer not live on the site
"Fastest fulfillment" or any superlative against competitors
Any efficacy, safety, outcome, dosing, or protocol statement
"We have not found another vendor publishing all 8" — the site's own line, but it is the Lanham Act exposure in a comparative ad
prohibited.comparative: Creatives that assert what a typical vendor does NOT do are comparative claims. Competitors stay unnamed, and the creative needs legal sign-off before it runs in PAID.

channelRules.$comment: See knowledge/compliance/NULUMIN_TIKTOK_PLAYBOOK.md. The paid/organic split is a compliance decision, not a style choice.
channelRules.paid: Research-use-only peptides have no lawful paid path on any major platform. Anything built with a shop CTA and an offer is for owned channels and email until that changes.
channelRules.organic: The documented enforcement vector for organic posts is COMMERCE SIGNALS — shop verbs, prices, offers, store links. Organic cuts carry none of them and swap the CTA for a non-commerce end card. Method education (what HPLC measures, what a lot number is for, what RUO means) is the one lane this category can post in at volume.
